title: Real customization of oscar.model.AbstractOption not possible
author: printshirt
body_preview: Summary I have tried to customize and override oscar.model.AbstractOption to set up a T-shirt printing service on the basis of Django Oscar. Obviously a T-shirt printing service requires the upload OPTION of an image, that the customer wants to have printed on the shirt. I do not doubt, that the Oscar overriding customization works for most requirements in other apps (basket, checkout, payment, .....

title: Dynamic Pricing (Price Lists) — buyer-aware base prices
author: maarcingebala
body_preview: ## Summary  This issue presents a plan for adding **buyer-aware base pricing** to Saleor: the ability to charge a different list price for the same variant depending on *who* is buying (e.g. VIP clients, wholesale) and *when* they're buying (e.g. a time-limited window price).  The feature is **opt-in and additive**. A store that never creates a tag or a scoped price row behaves exactly as it does...

title: Drop support for HS256 JWTs
author: NyanKiyoshi
body_preview: Saleor currently supports JWT signing using HS256 which uses `SECRET_KEY`. This requires a sufficiently strong secret thus making HS256 security dependent on the entropy and the adequate protection of that secret.  Instead, it would preferable to only allow RS256 in order to ensure the secret is sufficiently strong.  Proposal: fully drop HS256 in a new minor version. This will require users to ens...

title: Bug:updateMetadata / deleteMetadata accept unbounded list inputs for Checkout metadata
author: gurumurugan123
body_preview: ### What are you trying to achieve?  I investigated the checkout metadata GraphQL mutations and noticed that `updateMetadata` and `deleteMetadata` accept unbounded list inputs for Checkout and CheckoutLine metadata operations.  These mutations currently allow extremely large `input` and `keys` arrays without enforcing the documented maximum list size limit already used elsewhere in the codebase....

title: Bug: Checkout line mutations accept unbounded list inputs causing potential resource exhaustion
author: gurumurugan123
body_preview: ### What are you trying to achieve?  I investigated checkout GraphQL mutations and noticed that several checkout line operations accept unbounded list inputs without enforcing the existing recommended maximum limit of 100 items.  Large payloads containing thousands of checkout lines can trigger excessive database work, stock validation, pricing calculations, and memory usage in a single request....
